# The Harvest Moon That Never Fails

## Scripture
*"While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall not cease."* — Genesis 8:22 (ESV)

## Reflection
October's Harvest Moon rises low and golden, hanging heavy near the horizon like a lantern lit for late workers. For centuries, farmers relied on this moon's extra light to gather crops before frost. It arrives in the same season, year after year—not because farmers deserve it, but because God made a promise.

After the flood, when the earth seemed unreliable and every future uncertain, God set a covenant in the sky's rhythms: seedtime and harvest will not cease. That promise still holds tonight. The moon that lit ancient fields now lights ours. No panic in the heavens, no hesitation—just quiet, faithful rising.

We live in a world that often feels like floodwater—unstable, unpredictable. Yet God built faithfulness into creation itself. The seasons don't negotiate. The moon doesn't ask permission. They simply obey the One who set them in motion.

Maybe you're in a season of waiting—sowing tears, wondering if harvest will ever come. Look up at that golden moon. It's not an accident of gravity. It's a signature of a God who keeps His word, who promised that as long as earth remains, His faithfulness remains too.

Your harvest may not arrive on your schedule. But the God of Genesis 8:22 has never once missed a season. He won't start with yours.

## Prayer
Father, when my seasons feel uncertain, remind me of Your covenant in the sky. The moon rises faithfully—so will Your promises in my life. Give me patience to sow, trust to wait, and eyes to see Your hand in every season. In Jesus' name, Amen.
